clue.text: Old lady tucked into wicked things, this being a feast day?

indicators.note: something tucked into something else sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: candles are things with wicks, so 'wicked' is used literally
MA is a familiar name for one's mother, an old lady

explanation.surface: An elderly woman tucks into some naughty treats on a holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wicked' looks like a moral judgement, but here it simply means fitted with wicks, which is what the outer word describes.
explanation.definitionFit: Candlemas is the Christian festival on 2 February celebrating the Presentation of Christ, with candles blessed.

clue.text: They're proverbially poor children supported by posh children in organised crime

indicators.note: organised means put into a new order, so the letters get rearranged

blocks.note: CH is the standard abbreviation for children
U means upper-class, as in U and non-U
the same abbreviation again
taken as written

explanation.surface: Deprived youngsters are bankrolled by rich kids in a crime ring.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'supported by' puts CH above U; together with another CH they are mixed in among the letters of CRIME.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying 'as poor as church mice' makes these creatures the proverbial image of poverty.

clue.text: Lowest point in drain in need of repair

indicators.note: something in need of repair is broken, so its letters are to be put back together differently

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A plumber notes the bottom of a broken drain.
explanation.definitionFit: Nadir, from astronomy, means the point directly below the observer, and so the lowest point of anything.

clue.text: Draw left good swimmer last in relay

indicators.note: the last in a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: L is the usual abbreviation for left
an otter is an animal that swims well
the end of the word relay

explanation.surface: A relay team draws lots, the strong swimmer going last.
explanation.definitionFit: A lottery is a draw, a game of chance where winning tickets are picked out at random.

clue.text: Conventional place of refuge?

blocks.note: first meaning: moderate, avoiding extremes
second meaning: a traffic island in the centre of a street, where pedestrians take refuge

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful second reading: a pedestrian refuge sits literally in the centre of the carriageway.
explanation.definitionFit: Middle-of-the-road describes views or tastes that are mainstream and unadventurous, hence conventional.

clue.text: Flying solo, first up - is it in a famous plane?

indicators.note: flying suggests letters tossed about in the air and landing in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, every letter used

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a pioneering solo flight first took off in a celebrated aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface fits the answer neatly: Lindbergh flew solo across the Atlantic in 1927 in this aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spirit of St Louis was Charles Lindbergh's monoplane, flown on the first solo nonstop transatlantic crossing.

clue.text: Dissident bishop in part of film

indicators.note: one thing in another sits within it, so one piece is placed inside

blocks.note: a reel is a spool of film, one part of a movie
B is the chess notation for bishop

explanation.surface: A dissenting churchman appears in a section of a movie.
explanation.definitionFit: A dissident is someone who rebels against authority, so the two nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Became hostile, friend in Preminger film

blocks.note: to rise or rise up is to rebel against someone
bud is American slang for a pal

explanation.surface: A pal turned nasty while appearing in an Otto Preminger movie.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosebud is a 1975 thriller directed by Otto Preminger, as well as the famous last word of Citizen Kane.

clue.text: Fight involving cattle station that is to diversify

indicators.note: involving means including within itself, so the outer word wraps the other

blocks.note: a bout is a boxing match
a ranch is a farm for raising cattle

explanation.surface: A ranch caught up in a quarrel decides to expand into new business.
explanation.definitionFit: To branch out is to extend activities into new areas, like a tree sending out limbs.

clue.text: Departed behind schedule

blocks.note: first meaning: dead
second meaning: arriving after the expected time

explanation.walkthrough: 'Departed' reads like a train leaving, but it is the euphemism for someone who has died.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective covers both someone recently deceased and anything tardy or overdue.

clue.text: Raised saw made more modern

blocks.note: up as in raised, lifted higher
to see someone is to date them romantically

explanation.surface: A lifted saw has been given a modern makeover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' suggests a tool or seeing something; here it means went out with someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To update something is to bring it up to date, refreshing it with current features.

clue.text: Second name on it initially stumped worker

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word that follows
here on is read as placed onto and within, so pieces sit inside another

blocks.note: taken as written; it wraps the next two pieces
N is the abbreviation for name
the start of stumped
the worker ant is the crossword's usual worker

explanation.surface: A cricket worker is stumped in a split second.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stumped' suggests cricket or bafflement, but only its first letter is wanted; 'on' here works as a placement signal rather than a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An instant is a moment, a very brief span of time like a second.

clue.text: Swear remedy must involve sulphur

indicators.note: to involve is to include within, so the outer word wraps the other

blocks.note: a cure is a remedy
S is the chemical symbol for sulphur

explanation.surface: Someone insists a reliable treatment has to contain sulphur, or else they will swear.
explanation.definitionFit: To curse is to swear, to utter profanities in anger.

clue.text: Relaxed call, we might deduce?

blocks.note: first meaning: easy-going, unhurried
second meaning, read cryptically: the answer's first word written backwards is a word for phoning

explanation.walkthrough: Take the answer as an instruction: LAID set back reads DIAL, which is to call on the phone.
explanation.definitionFit: Laid-back is an informal adjective for a calm, unworried temperament.

clue.text: Ambassador, in December, somehow produces a delicacy

indicators.note: one thing in another sits within it, so the first piece goes inside the month
somehow suggests things arranged in some undetermined way, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written; it holds the next piece
HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador

explanation.surface: An ambassador's Christmas party serves up something special.
explanation.walkthrough: Bêche-de-mer is the sea cucumber, a dried delicacy prized in Chinese cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: Bêche-de-mer, the sea slug, is eaten as an expensive luxury food, especially in East Asia.

clue.text: Easy pickings, since elderly guy is after brass

blocks.note: brass is northern British slang for cash
for as a conjunction means because, since
a plain synonym
a guy is a rope that holds a tent steady

explanation.surface: An old man is easily exploited, because he is chasing money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is after' tells you the other pieces come after the word for brass, which therefore leads.
explanation.definitionFit: Money for old rope is an idiom for payment earned with little or no effort, so easy pickings.

clue.text: A political address?

blocks.note: surface reading: a speech given by a politician
setter's reading: the street address of a political figure's home, the British Prime Minister's residence in Downing Street

explanation.walkthrough: 'Address' suggests a speech; it is really the house number of the Prime Minister's London home.
explanation.definitionFit: Number Ten, 10 Downing Street, is the official residence and office of the British Prime Minister.

clue.text: Appear to score and fulfil an obligation

blocks.note: to come up is to appear or arise
taken as written
to score a surface is to scratch it

explanation.surface: A player seems set to score and do what is expected of them.
explanation.definitionFit: To come up to scratch is to reach the required standard, meeting what is demanded of you.

clue.text: Dirty seat over in a Parisian street

indicators.note: turned over in a down clue means read from the bottom up, so backwards
one thing in another sits within it, so a piece goes inside the street

blocks.note: un is French for a
a pew is a church bench
ST is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: A grubby bench lies tipped over in a street in Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: A floor that is unswept has not been cleaned with a broom, so it is dirty.

clue.text: I'm great playing Scott Joplin music

indicators.note: playing suggests letters moving about freely, so they are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A pianist boasts of their skill at performing Joplin's tunes.
explanation.definitionFit: Scott Joplin was the leading composer of ragtime, the syncopated piano style of around 1900.

clue.text: Cinema broadcast shows nervous wrens meeting slippery character

indicators.note: nervous birds flutter and fidget, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
an eel is notoriously slippery

explanation.surface: A cinema report shows jittery birds encountering a slippery customer.
explanation.definitionFit: A newsreel was a short filmed news bulletin shown in cinemas before the main feature.

clue.text: Confined to school, some cheating at Edmonton

indicators.note: some means a part of what follows, so the letters lie within the next words

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of cheating, all of at and the start of Edmonton

explanation.surface: A pupil caught cheating in Edmonton is kept in.
explanation.walkthrough: Gated is British school and university slang for being forbidden to leave the grounds as punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Being gated is a punishment that confines a student to college or school, like being grounded.

clue.text: Miserable time for returning flock

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so read backwards

blocks.note: poor as in wretched, pitiable
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A shepherd has a wretched time while the flock is coming home.
explanation.definitionFit: A troop is a group, and as a verb to flock or troop is to move together in a crowd.

clue.text: Motorway below remote croft

indicators.note: in a down clue, below means placed underneath, so the motorway piece is sent second

blocks.note: far as in distant
M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in M1

explanation.surface: A motorway runs beneath a remote smallholding.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'below' puts the motorway letter under FAR. A croft is a small Scottish farm.
explanation.definitionFit: A croft is a small rented farm in the Scottish Highlands, a kind of farm.

clue.text: Design style redcoat ordered

indicators.note: ordered means arranged into a sequence, so the letters are put in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written; a redcoat is a British soldier

explanation.surface: A British soldier commanded a particular style of decor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordered' reads as a redcoat ordering something; it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Art Deco is the geometric decorative design movement of the 1920s and 1930s.

clue.text: Identical costume

blocks.note: first meaning: the same throughout, consistent
second meaning: the standard outfit worn by members of a group

explanation.definitionFit: Uniform as an adjective means unvarying and alike; as a noun it is the regulation dress of a school or service.

clue.text: Painter meant to be different

indicators.note: being different means changing form, so the letters take another arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An artist was destined to stand apart from the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Édouard Manet was a nineteenth-century French painter, a forerunner of Impressionism.

clue.text: One's mood following onset of deadly viral illness

indicators.note: the onset is the beginning, so only the first letter is kept

blocks.note: the start of deadly
I is one, plus the S of the possessive
a temper is a state of mind or mood

explanation.surface: Someone's spirits sink as a lethal virus takes hold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' puts the opening letter of deadly first, before I'S and the mood word.
explanation.definitionFit: Distemper is a contagious viral disease of dogs and other animals.
